raw_response:
I farm only 9 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What feeds my family and brings cash is still the wheat-maize rotation, same as many people here. I have done this for 30 years, and I mostly follow what worked on my own land and what I see in the village. Wheat needs to be steady, so I will not save too much on fertilizer there. If the wheat turns yellow and weak, I lose more than the fertilizer money. Maize comes right after wheat, and the time is tight, so I keep it simple: harvest wheat, clear the field fast, do light tillage, then plant maize right away. We have a well, but pumping costs money, so I will water when the crop really needs it, not too many times. My family has 5 people, but some work outside, so I mostly count on family labor for the key days and hire a little help only if harvest and planting clash.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with improved local seed that people around here commonly use. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then give one topdressing around jointing if the crop looks like it needs it. I usually feel safer giving wheat a bit more than too little. For maize, I will use hybrid seed after wheat harvest in mid-June. I will not spend too much on maize fertilizer, but I still need enough so the ears fill well. If rain is decent, I reduce one irrigation. If it stays dry, I water from the well. I do not spray unless I see a real problem, but for weeds I usually use herbicide because family labor is limited.
